title: SQL Injection in VulnerableAppointmentRepository.findById
description: The findById method in VulnerableAppointmentRepository uses direct string concatenation to build SQL queries, making it vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. The method constructs a query by directly interpolating the user-supplied 'id' parameter into the SQL string without any sanitization or parameterization. An attacker can supply a malicious ID like '1' OR '1'='1' -- to bypass the WHERE clause and retrieve all appointments.
impact: Full appointment data exfiltration across all customers and barbers. An attacker can retrieve, modify, or delete appointments belonging to other users. Potential for data manipulation and privilege escalation through data manipulation.
mitigation: Replace string concatenation with parameterized queries using parameterized queries ($1, $2, etc.) as demonstrated in the findByIdSafe method. Use parameterized queries with the SqlExecutor's queryOne method that accepts parameters array.

history.details: Initial audit finding recorded for SQL injection in findById method

Determined status as VALID because Confirmed SQL injection in findById method at line 27: direct string concatenation of user-supplied 'id' parameter into SQL query without parameterization. Test confirms exploitability via sql-injection.test.ts line 122-141 showing successful injection returning CONFIRMED appointments.

Determined production viability as SAMPLE_OR_TEST because KB freshness gate passes (KB_SNAPSHOT: snap_20250829_01 == active SNAPSHOT_ID: snap_20250829_01). Threat model declares Intent: SAMPLE_OR_TEST_ONLY - this is an educational Security Lab with intentionally vulnerable API (api-vulnerable) for training. All findings reside in intentionally vulnerable demo code, not production deployable artifacts.
